questions.question: Under product-probability factorization, what composition rule does the paper derive for Mathai's non-additive discrete entropy?
questions.rationale: Equation (11) has a bilinear correction proportional to α−1; additivity is recovered at α=1.

questions.question: Which of the listed generalized entropies remains additive under PPP because its composition coefficient a(α) is zero?
questions.rationale: The table gives a(α)=0 for M* as well as Rényi; the other listed choices have nonzero coefficients generally.

questions.question: What does the authors' criticism of the usual independence definition using the sure event illustrate?

options.A: Every pair of disjoint events has product probability
options.B: No events can be independent unless the sample space is infinite
options.C: The definition makes any event independent of the sure event, which they argue conflicts with ordinary intuition
options.D: Equal-probability elementary outcomes are incompatible with PPP

questions.rationale: They point out that P(A∩S)=P(A)P(S) always holds, despite A being contained in S, and use this to motivate the term PPP.
questions.evidence_quote: any event A ∈ S, and S the sure event are independent.

questions.question: In the authors' account of Shannon entropy's additivity, what assumption is doing the conceptual work beyond PPP itself?

options.A: A requirement that all marginal probabilities be uniform
options.B: A constraint on the variance of the joint distribution
options.C: A restriction to two-event sample spaces
options.D: A recursivity postulate that yields a logarithmic functional form

questions.rationale: They argue logarithms turn products into sums and that the recursivity postulate introduces this logarithmic form.
questions.evidence_quote: the nature of the recursivity postulate automatically determines the logarithmic functional form for Shannon entropy.

questions.question: For a trivariate PPP distribution, how does the generalized entropy's highest-order interaction term depend on a(α)?

options.A: It is [a(α)]² times the product of all three marginal entropies
options.B: It is linear in a(α) and contains a sum of the three marginal entropies
options.C: It vanishes only when all three marginals are identical
options.D: It is a(α) times the joint entropy itself

questions.rationale: Equation (14) includes pairwise terms proportional to a(α) and a triple-product term proportional to its square.

questions.question: When maximizing the continuous Mathai entropy under a fixed ordinary δ-moment, which parameter regime yields a generalized type-1 beta pathway density?

options.A: α>1 with the bracket 1−s(α−1)x^δ and unrestricted support
options.B: α<1 with the bracket 1−s(1−α)x^δ and positive support

questions.rationale: Equation (31) gives type-1 beta for α<1, with support restricted by positivity of the bracket.
questions.evidence_quote: For α < 1 or −∞ < α < 1 the right side of (31) remains as a generalized type-1 beta model

questions.question: What pathway-family limit does the paper obtain as α approaches 1 in the scalar model with exponent δ?

options.A: A uniform distribution on a finite interval
options.C: A stretched exponential proportional to exp(−s x^δ)
options.D: A point mass at the origin

questions.rationale: The limit of the generalized beta pathway density is the extended/stretched exponential.
questions.evidence_quote: When α → 1 in (31) or in (32) we have an extended or stretched exponential form

questions.question: For the pathway model f(x)=c x^(γ−1)[1−s(1−α)x^δ]^(1/(1−α)), what family is obtained for α>1?
questions.rationale: For α>1, rewriting 1−α=−(α−1) produces the type-2 beta form.
questions.evidence_quote: For α > 1, writing 1 − α = −(α − 1) the model in (31) goes to a generalized type-2 beta form

questions.question: What is the specific mathematical limitation the authors acknowledge in the event-independence argument based on equally likely elementary outcomes?

options.A: They show no integer solutions in the example for some n such as 3, 5, and 7, not a universal impossibility
options.B: They prove the absence of independent events for every sample-space size
options.C: They assume nonuniform elementary outcomes, invalidating the conclusion
options.D: They restrict the argument to continuous random variables

questions.rationale: The text gives selected n values as examples and frames the reasoning around symmetric finite sample spaces; it is not a universal theorem that independence never occurs.
questions.evidence_quote: There is no solution for x, y, z for a large number of n, for example, n = 3, 5, 7.

questions.question: For which parameter choices does the paper identify the pathway model's α→1 limit as the Gaussian density?

options.B: γ=1, δ=2 on the full real line

questions.rationale: The paper identifies γ=1 and δ=2 on the full real line as the Gaussian case.
questions.evidence_quote: for δ = 2, γ = 1, α → 1, −∞ < x < ∞ is the Gaussian density
